segments.caption: Adelaide. December 2014.
Two weeks earlier, in Sydney, Phillip Hughes was batting on 63, when a bouncer hit him on the neck. Two days later, he was gone. He was 25.
Now the first Test of the summer comes to Adelaide. The ground he called home.
Before a ball is bowled, the whole ground rises, and claps, for 63 seconds.
This is the Adelaide Test.
Day one. Australia bat. They wear black armbands, and 408, Hughes's Test cap number, on their shirts.
David Warner, Hughes's friend, reaches 63, and looks to the sky. He goes on to 145.
Michael Clarke can barely bend. His back gives way on 60. He retires hurt.
Australia close the day on 354 for 6.
Day two. Clarke walks back out. He will call it the most important Test of his career.
He makes 128. Steve Smith, 162 not out.
Australia declare on 517 for 7.
Day three. MS Dhoni is injured. India's stand-in captain is Virat Kohli. 26, the age Hughes would have turned, just days before this Test.
He walks in at 111 for 2. The first ball from Mitchell Johnson hits him on the helmet.
The ground falls silent. Australia's players rush to him. Johnson looks shaken. Clarke puts a hand on his shoulder.
Kohli gets up. And makes 115.
India finish on 444, 73 behind. Nathan Lyon takes five.
Day four. Warner makes his second hundred of the match. Australia declare overnight.
India need 364, on the final day, on a turning pitch.
Most teams would block for a draw. India go for it.
Day five. Shikhar Dhawan goes early. Cheteshwar Pujara follows. 57 for 2.
Then Kohli and Murali Vijay start to believe.
They take India to tea on 205 for 2. 159 to win, in a session.
Kohli reaches a second hundred. Only Greg Chappell had ever made twin hundreds in his first Test as captain.
The stand reaches 185. 242 for 2. 122 to win. Eight wickets in hand.
Then, Nathan Lyon.
Vijay, lbw, for 99.
Same over. Ajinkya Rahane is given out caught, off his pad. There is no review system in this series.
Rohit Sharma falls. Wriddhiman Saha swings, and is bowled.
And on 141, Kohli goes for one more big hit, and is caught by Mitchell Marsh.
From 242 for 2, India lose eight wickets for 73. The last man is stumped. Lyon, again.
Australia win by 48 runs. Lyon takes 7 for 152, and 12 in the match.
Kohli's 256 runs are the most by an Indian in his first Test as captain. Within a month, the job is his for good.
India lose the Test. But they find their captain.
Some Tests are won. This one is remembered.
63, not out. Forever.
Beyond The Scoreboard.
